subject.title: Improve doctor/gateway diagnostics clarity for mixed LaunchAgent/runtime states

question: What final `openclaw doctor` diagnosis taxonomy and recovery-order output should OpenClaw standardize for mixed LaunchAgent, runtime, RPC, service-drift, and channel-conflict states?
rationale: Current main already gathers many underlying facts, but the public wording, state precedence, action ordering, and optional machine-readable diagnosis block are operator-facing product choices that automation should not invent.

options.title: Compose final doctor verdict
options.body: Add a final healthy/degraded/down diagnosis with probable causes and ordered next steps, reusing existing service/runtime/RPC/channel facts.

options.title: Keep independent panels
options.body: Leave doctor output as separate panels and only improve individual confusing messages after a live transcript proves a specific case.

options.title: Design structured diagnosis first
options.body: Define a compact diagnosis object first, then render prose and optional JSON output from that object in a later implementation.

recommendation.title: Compose final doctor verdict
recommendation.body: Add a final healthy/degraded/down diagnosis with probable causes and ordered next steps, reusing existing service/runtime/RPC/channel facts.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is repeated work on doctor orchestration, LaunchAgent recovery, and gateway probe diagnostics in the central paths.
